sections.text_helper: Section 48.4.8 "SAES suspend and resume operations" in chapter 48 (Secure AES coprocessor (SAES)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 2310.
sections.section_content:
A message can be suspended to process another message with a higher priority. When the
higher-priority message is sent, the suspended message can resume. This applies to both
encryption and decryption mode.
Suspend and resume operations do not break the chaining operation. The message
processing can resume as soon as SAES is enabled again, to receive a next data block.
The suspend and resume operations are only supported when SAES is used in CPU mode,
not in DMA mode.
Figure458 gives an example of suspend and resume operations: Message 1 is suspended
in order to send a shorter and higher-priority Message 2.
[Figure 458. Example of suspend mode management]
...
A detailed description of suspend and resume operations is in the sections dedicated to
each chaining mode.
